prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The best candidate (c006, CTS cluster_size=1/diameter=50) reduced upper-tier moderate violations by making the clock tree flatter; combine it with a second independent, already-validated-in-spirit mechanism — relaxing global-route congestion iterations so GRT converges to a lower-overflow solution (overflow is a hard constraint and routed parasitics feed the final STA) — by raising congestion_iterations from 2 to 4 in the shared global_route.tcl, which reduces detoured/overflowing nets and thus improves post-route parasitics without touching per-circuit knobs.
Rule-based digest:
total=-inf robust(mean-std)=-inf min_case=-inf all_valid=False
  failures: bp_fe-ng45/1001:stage timeout; bp_fe-ng45/1002:stage timeout; bp_fe-ng45/1003:KeyError in partition; bp-ng45/1001:stage timeout; bp-ng45/1002:HBT min-spacing violation; bp-ng45/1003:KeyError in partition
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Invalid: mixed timeout (bp_fe-ng45 1001/1002, bp-ng45 1001), crash (KeyError in partition, 1003 both), and legality (HBT min-spacing, bp-ng45 1002). Timeouts hit all seeds of two cases → systematic; KeyErrors also systematic per case. So this candidate says nothing about the hypothesis. Likely the raised congestion_iterations blew runtime and perturbed partitioning/legality. Make it legal: keep iterations=4 but add a GRT runtime cap/early-exit on overflow convergence, and gate the change behind a per-design check so partition/HBT cases aren't affected; rerun.
